It uses the original fixed Haar/cap normalization once. The regular pole
has k~kappa rho^6, e~kappa rho^4. Thus

```
alpha=(sqrt(37)-5)/2,
alpha(alpha+5)=3,
u_regular~rho^alpha,
u_singular~rho^(-5-alpha).
```

The singular homogeneous solution has infinite form energy. Define V_0
as the regular Friedrichs form closure with zero outer trace, keeping the
actual weighted derivative/angular norms. If k/rho^6 and e/rho^4 are bounded
above and below by finite positive constants on this physical radial domain,
the form is closed/coercive on V_0. A source in V_0* and a finite-energy trace
lift therefore define a unique weak Dirichlet application. This proves a
conditional scalar-block result, not full physical Cauchy well-posedness.

An explicit dense regular core is generated by

```
x=rho/R,
b_j=x^alpha (1-x) P_j^(2,4+2alpha)(2x-1),  j=0,1,...,
trace lift l=x^alpha.
```

No finite j cutoff is selected. This is a core/form closure: it does not
force every inhomogeneously sourced solution to have exactly the homogeneous
pointwise leading power. Cutoffs near the pole and polynomial approximation
